header.title: GST MCP Server
header.ledeAfter: with your AI agents. Supercharge your analysis to accelerate and lower costs of decision-making.
what.heading: What it does
what.lede: Your analysts already screen targets, portfolio companies and deals with AI agents; connect those AI agents to GST's MCP server to accelerate assessment, benchmarking, and project administration.
what.case1.title: Deal Screening
what.case1.body: During initial screening, an analyst's agent calls the diligence agenda tool with the target's profile and returns a starter agenda the IC memo is built around, recovering 2 to 4 hours per screened deal.
what.case2.title: Cost Benchmarking
what.case2.body: A portfolio operating partner benchmarks total technology spend against stage-adjusted ranges and prices the carrying cost of technical debt, turning "engineering feels slow" into a number the board can act on.
what.case3.title: Regulatory Exposure
what.case3.body: Before bidding on a healthtech target, an agent scopes which frameworks are in play by jurisdiction and effective date, so counsel starts from an exposure list instead of an open question.
what.case4.title: Programmatic Access
what.case4.body: A client's internal tooling (Retool, a Slack bot, a custom dashboard) calls the server directly, treating GST's frameworks as a managed API rather than a site somebody has to visit.
exposed.heading: What's exposed
exposed.note: The server implements all three MCP server primitives: Tools, Resources, and Prompts. Together they give an agent what a good analyst needs on day one: instruments to run the numbers, the reference material to run them against, and a method for what order to do it in.
primitives.tools.heading: Tools
primitives.tools.def: The work an associate would otherwise build in a spreadsheet, or wait on an advisor to deliver. Each tool runs a GST model against your deal's parameters and returns figures defensible enough for an IC memo: a scoped diligence agenda, a cost benchmark, a debt estimate, a regulatory exposure list. The model invokes them on its own as the conversation calls for them, so an analyst asks in plain English instead of learning an API. Radar tools are granted separately.
primitives.resources.heading: Resources
primitives.resources.def: The frameworks behind the numbers, readable in full. An agent working from GST's actual VDR taxonomy, diligence checklists, and regulation corpus grounds its answers in a published method rather than in whatever it absorbed during training, which is the difference between a citation you can check and a confident guess. The host application loads these as context, so they are in the conversation before the model needs them.
primitives.prompts.heading: Prompts
primitives.prompts.def: Knowing which tool to call is not the hard part. Knowing the order is, and that is what a firm's experience actually buys. Each prompt captures a GST workflow as a sequence, so a first-year associate running a diligence kickoff follows the same progression a GST engagement would. They surface as slash commands in the client, chosen deliberately by a person rather than guessed at by a model.
catalog.tools.agenda.title: Diligence agenda
catalog.tools.agenda.gloss: Turns a target profile into a prioritized diligence agenda with scope and timeline estimates.
catalog.tools.history.title: Engagement history
catalog.tools.history.gloss: Searches GST's engagement record by sector, deal type, stage, and scale, and lists the values each filter accepts.
catalog.tools.regulatory.title: Regulatory exposure
catalog.tools.regulatory.gloss: Queries {count} regulatory frameworks by jurisdiction, category, and effective date.
catalog.tools.infra.title: Infrastructure cost
catalog.tools.infra.gloss: Scores cloud cost governance maturity across six domains and returns a prioritized improvement list.
catalog.tools.spend.title: Technology spend
catalog.tools.spend.gloss: Benchmarks total technology cost against stage-adjusted ranges and projects a 36-month trajectory.
catalog.tools.debt.title: Technical debt
catalog.tools.debt.gloss: Estimates the annual carrying cost of technical debt from team size, salary, and delivery metrics.
catalog.tools.irl.title: Information requests
catalog.tools.irl.gloss: Builds a fillable information request list, populates it from evidence already in hand, then ingests the completed file and checks every answer back to its source.
catalog.tools.radar.title: Radar search
catalog.tools.radar.gloss: Searches curated PE, M&A, and enterprise-technology intelligence, filtered by category and recency.
catalog.resources.library.title: Library
catalog.resources.library.gloss: The reference guides behind GST's diligence method, in full.
catalog.resources.regulations.title: Regulatory frameworks
catalog.resources.regulations.gloss: One document per framework, each with its requirements, penalties, and effective dates.
catalog.resources.radar.title: Radar feeds
catalog.resources.radar.gloss: FYI carries GST-annotated highlights; Wire carries the full stream, whole or by category.
catalog.prompts.deal.title: Deal workflow
catalog.prompts.deal.gloss: Open a diligence engagement, size up a target quickly, and produce the memos a deal team hands onward.
catalog.prompts.irl.title: Information requests
catalog.prompts.irl.gloss: Issue a request list to a target, populate it from evidence in hand, then sweep what comes back into a cited dossier without rekeying it.
catalog.prompts.review.title: Review & briefing
catalog.prompts.review.gloss: Standing reviews: architecture by layer, regulatory exposure, and the day's radar.
tiers.heading: Capability tiers
tiers.note: Tiers differ by who is using the server and how broadly, not by which tools you get. Scopes are set per client during provisioning.
tiers.pilot.name: Pilot
tiers.pilot.note: Evaluation access for a single team. Narrow scopes, radar excluded by default.
tiers.paid.name: Deal Team
tiers.paid.note: Production access for a deal team, invoiced per agreement.
tiers.enterprise.name: Firm
tiers.enterprise.note: Firm-wide access across multiple clients, compliance capabilities on request.
tiers.callout.title: On these numbers
tiers.callout.body: These are tunable, non-contractual capability ceilings, NOT ratified SLA quotas. They are abuse and capacity limits, adjustable per client, and nothing here is a promised allowance.
access.heading: How access works
access.provisioning.label: Provisioning
access.provisioning.item1: Access is operator-provisioned. There is no self-serve signup and no dynamic client registration. A client record is created by GST, with scopes and a tier assigned deliberately.
access.provisioning.item2: Radar tools are granted separately and are excluded from a typical grant, because they draw on a shared third-party research budget.
access.auth.label: Authentication
access.auth.item1: Machine-to-machine clients authenticate with OAuth 2.1 client_credentials, using a client secret or a registered signing key.
access.auth.item2: The interactive authorization-code flow, for a person connecting Claude on the web or Desktop or another AI client, requires PKCE with S256, with no exceptions and no plaintext challenge.
access.ops.label: Operations
access.ops.item1: A tamper-evident, hash-chained audit log with seven-year retention exists as built-and-tested capability. It is activated for a client whose contract requires it, as part of onboarding.
access.ops.item2: Operational health (dependency status, per-tool latency, request volume) is published on the status page.
engineers.heading: For your engineers
engineers.lede: One endpoint to configure, once a client record exists. Credentials arrive with provisioning.
guides.heading: Guides
guides.note: Four guides take a provisioned client from credential to everyday use: connect the server, drive it well, ingest a completed information request list, and look up any capability's contract.
guides.getStarted.title: Get started
guides.getStarted.blurb: Connector setup for Claude on the web and Claude Desktop: prerequisites, quick start, and how to verify the connection.
guides.using.title: Using the server
guides.using.blurb: First query, prompt argument forms, pinned resources, and what each failure means.
guides.advanced.title: Advanced operations
guides.advanced.blurb: Ingest a completed information request list and drive nine engines in one turn.
guides.docs.title: Documentation
guides.docs.blurb: Every capability's contract: arguments, a worked example, what comes back, and which workflows use it.
request.heading: Request access
request.note: Tell GST who you are, what you are building, and roughly how much you expect to call. Provisioning is a conversation, not a signup form, which is also how scopes and a tier get set correctly the first time.
